questions.q: Which of these is known for sure a year in advance?
options: Day of week of a date
why: Weather is only forecast, not known.

questions.q: Why does target encoding on all rows leak?
options: Each row's own target (and later targets) is inside its feature
why: Correct: the feature contains information from the row's target and from the future.

questions.q: Store A sales in time order: 10, 30, 20. Safe expanding encoding for row 3?
questions.why: Earlier rows are 10 and 30. The mean is 20.

questions.q: Smoothed encoding: sum of earlier targets = 40, count = 2, prior (overall mean so far) = 30, smoothing m = 2. What is the value? (sum + m*prior) / (count + m)
Select all features that are safe to use for a forecast of next month's demand.
options: Actual sales of the target month
Public holiday list for next year
why: Yes, if the promotions are planned before the forecast is made.
Yes. Holiday lists are published in advance.

questions.q: You encode day of week as the numbers 0 to 6 in a linear regression, and Sunday errors are large. What is a better encoding?
options: Use one-hot columns or sin/cos features
why: A single number still forces a straight-line effect.
Correct: each day gets its own effect, or the cycle is represented smoothly.
The weekly pattern is usually strong, so dropping it loses information.

questions.q: Holiday dates: Easter changes every year. Your training data covers 2021 to 2023 and you forecast 2024. What is the right approach?
options: Use the Easter date of 2023 for 2024
Use a holiday table that contains the exact date for each year, including 2024
why: Easter moves, so the date is wrong.
Correct: the holiday calendar is known for the future years.
Easter has a strong effect on many businesses.
